car_01.title: Car 01. Brake van
car_01.shani.greet_known: Ah, it's you. I said I'd wait.
car_01.shani.stage.crate: Sits on a crate by the regulator. Looks not at you but at the needle.
car_01.shani.who: He does not introduce himself. The clock above him stands at half past eight.
car_01.shani.look_ok: You have seen that limp before. At the bend, by the black stone. He knows it, and he does not care.
car_01.shani.look_fail: A face like any face. The lantern's shadow cuts it in two, and the halves do not meet.
car_01.shani.silent: Good. Only those with nowhere to go hurry here.
npc.god_shani.name: Lame man in dark clothes
npc.god_shani.axis.recorded: You are on record. So they will look for you. That is neither good nor bad.
npc.god_shani.axis.unrecorded: You are in no book. So there is no one to lose you.
npc.god_shani.axis.uniform: A uniform. Back here, in the tail, it weighs nothing.
npc.god_shani.axis.rags: That is what one boards the tail in. You are in the right place.
npc.god_shani.axis.woman: You are late, madam. Do sit.
npc.bir_singh.name: Bir Singh, conductor
npc.kanu.name: Kanu
npc.ratan.name: Ratan Mondol
npc.saraswati.name: Saraswati
npc.hafiz.name: Hafiz-sahib
npc.dog.name: The dog
npc.monimala.name: Monimala Devi
lhh.title: The Last Half Hour
lhh.intro: Eight in the evening. The ticket is in your inside pocket, the luggage by the door. Howrah is twenty minutes away — you know it, the servant knows it, the cabman knows it. We'll make it.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.text: “They're after me. Crane's men. Hide me — till morning, no more.” He coughs into his fist, and the cough sounds as if something inside were glowing.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.stage: The centrifuge worker from the Salkia strike. Holds his chest. Something flat under his shirt.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.hide.out: You show him the gap behind the woodpile. He takes a notebook from under his shirt — hours, names, everyone who worked the centrifuges — and puts it back. “I'll go in the morning. The train will wait.” It won't. But he will ride.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.dodge: Get out of it: not here, not tonight.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.dodge.out: You find the words. He nods and goes down the lane. A block on, two men turn after him. The notebook is on him.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.dodge.fail: The words don't come. He stands in the gate and won't go until they come for him themselves. You watch him taken, and it takes longer than helping would have.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.push.out: You shove, and he doesn't resist — only looks. The workers on the corner saw. The word will reach the works before the train does.
lhh.d.nibaron_das.push.fail: The shove is weak, he grabs your sleeve, and you stand in full view of the street until they take him. Worse than anything — and longer.
lhh.d.shoshibhushon_mitra.text: “The doctor asked me to pass it on. If anyone asked. You were at the lecture.” He pushes a notebook in an oilcloth cover at you, not meeting your eyes.
lhh.d.shoshibhushon_mitra.stage: A small, polite, frightened clerk of the Association. Umbrella under his arm. Keeps looking round.
lhh.d.shoshibhushon_mitra.take.out: The notebook is heavier than it looks. Calculations that don't add up — you'll understand that in eighty hours. Shoshibhushon is already running, and he is lighter.
lhh.d.shoshibhushon_mitra.refuse.out: He hides the notebook again and goes, hunched. Where he puts it — you'll see. Not tonight.
lhh.d.shoshibhushon_mitra.force: Take it. He won't hand it over nicely.
lhh.d.shoshibhushon_mitra.force.out: The notebook is yours, his umbrella is broken. He doesn't shout. He remembers — and there is someone to tell.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.text: “Crate four-twelve. You touched it. A shortfall. I need your signature — or an explanation.” He sweats and looks over his spectacles.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.stage: Clerk of the opium warehouse, a Marwari, ledger under his arm.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.blame.out: You sign. He exhales as if a crate were lifted off his shoulders. In the opium car they will treat you as one of their own — and as one who knows how to keep quiet.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.see_through: Look closer: why is he sweating so?
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.see_through.out: He made the shortfall himself. You say it quietly, and he stops sweating — he simply goes white. Now he is your debtor, and for a long time.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.see_through.fail: Something about him is wrong, but you can't catch it. The argument drags, and in the end you sign half of what he wanted. He leaves unhappy — and so do you.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.push: Push past. Find your signature elsewhere.
lhh.d.ramkishen_agarwal.push.out: The ledger falls in the dust. He picks it up and says, “I'll open a file.” He will.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.text: “I'm going to the station. Same as you. Help me carry it. I can't hold it alone.” The urn is wrapped in white and warm, as if something inside still smoulders.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.stage: The widow from the ghat. Going to Benares, third class.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.carry: Take the urn and walk beside her.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.carry.out: You carry her ashes, she carries your bag, and so you walk all the way to Howrah. On the train she will sit where you sit. You will not be alone.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.other_car: Put her in another carriage and go your own way.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.other_car.out: You find her a place in third class and a cab to the station. She thanks you coldly. She understood what you did.
lhh.d.widow_monimala.pass.out: You walk on. She stands with the urn in the middle of the street, and you don't look back. She will not make this train.
lhh.d.sher_ali.text: “Brother! Where are you going? Sit. I haven't finished about Kabul.” He hugs your shoulders and won't let go. He is not retired. He looks at you with the eyes of a man whose regiment is on this very train.
lhh.d.sher_ali.stage: The sepoy from Bowbazar. Drunk, happy, and he knows you.
lhh.d.sher_ali.listen: Hear the Kabul story to the end.
lhh.d.sher_ali.listen.out: The story is long, and at its end there is no regiment — there is a night, a gorge, and one man who walked away. He told you. No one else.
lhh.d.sher_ali.talk: Talk him round: he'll finish another time.
lhh.d.sher_ali.talk.out: You promise to hear the rest on the train. He believes you and lets go. Tomorrow he won't know you — and that may be better for him.
lhh.d.sher_ali.talk.fail: He won't let go. He takes offence, then cries, then hugs you again. You leave when he falls asleep standing.
lhh.d.sher_ali.patrol: Call the patrol: let them take him.
lhh.d.sher_ali.patrol.out: The patrol takes him by the arms. He looks back at you once. In the regimental car they will know.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.text: “This is written against you. Twelve rupees. Not your debt? It's written against you. Who pays?” The ledger is strapped in leather. The real debtor died a month ago — he knows it, but the ledger does not forgive.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.stage: A Kabuliwala. Tall, turbaned, debt ledger on a strap.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.pay.out: He counts twice and strikes the line through. “Now I remember you.” In third class, if it comes to wagers, he will bet on you.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.acknowledge.out: He writes under your name: “acknowledged”. A short word, and it will stretch through half the train.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.refuse: Refuse: not your debt, not your concern.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.refuse.out: He looks for a long time. Then closes the ledger. Not strikes through — closes. In Murugan's car he will testify against you.
lhh.d.gul_mohammad.refuse.fail: Your voice fails. He doesn't leave until he has heard everything — and remembered everything. He will testify in detail.
lhh.d.ah_sun.text: “Your order. Not finished. You're leaving — take it as it is, the balance later.” The parcel smells of glue, and something inside glints like glass.
lhh.d.ah_sun.stage: The craftsman from Tiretta Bazaar. Cut hands, the shop behind him still open.
lhh.d.ah_sun.wait: Wait while he finishes the real one.
lhh.d.ah_sun.wait.out: He is angry at himself and works fast. A small crystal — real, three charges — lands warm in your palm. “Patient. I'll remember.”
lhh.d.ah_sun.fake.out: Glass. Pretty, faceted, with a vein. Once it will fool a detector. Not twice.
lhh.d.ah_sun.leave: Leave: he can keep the balance.
lhh.d.ah_sun.leave.out: He doesn't argue. In the opium car his name will be spoken in front of you — with contempt, and that will be your doing.
lhh.d.sidi_bilal.text: “Read it. Nobody reads to me. Is it about me — or not about me?” A stamped sheet. He cannot read, and he suspects what it says.
lhh.d.sidi_bilal.stage: A lascar from Kidderpore, a Habshi, fifty or so. Hands scarred by ropes.
lhh.d.sidi_bilal.read: Read it as it is. All of it.
lhh.d.sidi_bilal.read.out: Discharged ashore without pay. You read to the end, he nods at every line as at verse. “Thank you. Now I know where I am.” His countrymen in the docks will remember.
lhh.d.sidi_bilal.lie.out: He smiles for the first time in the conversation. You leave quickly. This lie will live to the epilogue.
lhh.d.sidi_bilal.refuse.out: He folds the sheet and puts it away. In Kala Pani he will be silent, and the silence will be about you.
lhh.d.pereira.text: “You answered wrong yesterday. Column ‘occupation’. A signature under the correction — two minutes.” It is never two minutes. The column is wrong — and he put you there himself, to close a shortfall.
lhh.d.pereira.stage: An Anglo-Indian, junior census taker, worn frock coat, a folder.
lhh.d.pereira.fix: Read it, find the error and demand it be corrected.
lhh.d.pereira.fix.out: You find the column and the class number. He reddens and rewrites. Now the record is right — the only clean ledger you will have.
lhh.d.pereira.fix.fail: You read and can't see the catch. You sign a correction that corrects nothing. The time is gone; the record isn't.
lhh.d.pereira.sign.out: You sign something that contradicts your ticket. Who notices first — a guard or an ethnographer — you'll learn in car twenty-two.
lhh.d.pereira.tear.out: The paper tears easily. You are not in the census. That will be an advantage exactly until the moment you need to exist.
lhh.d.sister_rosario.text: “Ice. What you bought today has melted, and there's cholera on the ward. More. As much as you can.” The patient the ice was for has already died. She takes it for the next.
lhh.d.sister_rosario.stage: A Goan nun from the Howrah hospital, apron stained.
lhh.d.sister_rosario.ice: Give the ice and buy more.
lhh.d.sister_rosario.ice.out: The ice goes to the hospital in your cab. In the train's infirmary they will treat you free — to the end.
lhh.d.sister_rosario.money.out: She takes the rupee without counting. “God sees.” Perhaps He does. The infirmary will remember it warmly.
lhh.d.sister_rosario.refuse.out: She doesn't argue. She goes. When cholera starts on the train, you will be refused a place in the queue — politely.
lhh.d.horipod.text: “Is this yours? No? And this?” Someone else's trunk on his shoulder, your bag under his arm, and he is honestly sure it is the other way round.
lhh.d.horipod.stage: A porter. The only honest man on this list.
lhh.d.horipod.sort: Sort it out together, bag by bag.
lhh.d.horipod.sort.out: Three strangers' suitcases, one of yours. One stranger's trunk rides with you anyway — its owner will find it in the luggage car. Horipod thanks you as if you had saved his job.
lhh.d.horipod.own.out: The bag is yours. The rest is his concern. He nods and hauls on.
lhh.d.horipod.steal: Take the stranger's trunk. It's heavier — so there's more in it.
lhh.d.horipod.steal.out: The trunk is someone else's, and the car it rides to will remember. Horipod didn't notice. Yet.
lhh.leg.ghat: Streets down to the river. A lamplighter with a ladder, the smell of silt, the boatmen's cries. Lights on the far bank.
lhh.crossing.text: The Hooghly. Howrah is on the far bank. Over the water by the Salkia centrifuge station the lamps burn a steady white — not the yellow every lamp in the world burns. The pontoon bridge, the ferry, the boats.
lhh.crossing.bridge.note: The bridge opens for ships. The later you arrive, the likelier.
lhh.crossing.boat_marwari: Hire a boat. Haggle — two annas.
lhh.crossing.boat_armenian: Hire a boat. Pay without looking — six annas.
lhh.bridge.open: The bridge is closed to ships. The planking hums underfoot; black water turns beneath it. You are alone on the whole bridge.
lhh.bridge.raised: The bridge is open: a jute barge goes upstream slowly, like a funeral. You wait. So does the clock over the watch-house.
lhh.ferry.bipin: “The Mail too? Third class, me. On business.” He says “on business” a shade too loudly. “Keep close to the tail — they say they board there without questions.”
lhh.ferry.stage: A clerk from Dalhousie, carefully dressed, one suitcase. Looks at your ticket as if he had seen it before.
lhh.boat.text: Bhagirath pushes off with the pole and whispers a prayer. The words go into the air above the water and do not come back. He repeats it louder. Then falls silent. Nobody says anything.
lhh.boat.bipin: In the stern, a clerk with one suitcase. “The Mail too? Bipin Chondro, Dalhousie. Third class.” He doesn't look at the boatman. He looks at the water over which nothing works.
lhh.boat.caught: “Out. Pay or get out.” You get out midstream, knee-deep in silt. A second boat takes you out of pity — and slower.
lhh.leg.shrine: The climb to the station. At the bend, right by the tracks — something black and glossy in the lamplight.
lhh.shrine.text: A roadside shrine: a black stone, oil, iron. Not a single flower. By the stone sits a lame man in dark clothes. He asks for nothing.
lhh.shrine.stage: The shrine's yard was drained first: the Salkia station is two steps away. It is quiet here in a way it never is.
lhh.shrine.dog: A hundred paces on, a dog throws itself under your feet — silent, no bark. You fall. The dog doesn't leave: it follows, a little way behind. It cost exactly what the oil would have.
lhh.shrine.spoke: “Straight on. Where the yellow ones stop burning.” He looks at your face longer than an answer needs.
lhh.leg.station: Howrah. Announcements in four languages, coolies, the pointer board, a crowd that does not part.
lhh.howrah.ladies: The ladies' waiting room: a separate entrance, a shorter queue, a polite guard — and twice as far to the right platform.
lhh.howrah.officer: “So it's you! Didn't think I'd catch you. Two minutes, just two.” He speaks politely and at length, and not listening is against regulations.
lhh.howrah.chinese: Nobody writes you down. Nobody stops you. Nobody sees you. It is the fastest of all — and it is also a way of slowing you down.
lhh.howrah.search: “Luggage.” The constable lays your things on the table one by one and puts them back in the wrong order.
lhh.howrah.babu: You know whom to ask. The station babu knows that you know. Tea is served. While the tea cools, the train raises steam.
lhh.howrah.marwari: The guard knows your firm. He checks the luggage against the waybill as slowly as if the waybill were his own. You name a fair price for his time — he pretends not to hear.
lhh.howrah.armenian: Your family has had an account here since the seventeenth century, and the guard knows it. He is polite. Politeness takes as long as a search.
lhh.howrah.anglo: The guard recognises one of his own. It doesn't help: he keeps you longer, so no one thinks he helped.
lhh.howrah.baghdadi: You know what this train carries better than the man checking your luggage. You say nothing. So does he — slowly.
lhh.howrah.dutch: The British guard reads your surname twice and grows a degree colder. A defeated empire passes, but not quickly.
lhh.howrah.queue: A queue. Just a queue, without a name or a face. It moves, but not towards you.
lhh.howrah.loafer_papers: “Act of sixty-nine. Papers.” You show them. The constable reads slowly, with his lips, checks against something in a book. Lets you go.
lhh.howrah.loafer_talk: “Act of sixty-nine. European vagrancy. Papers.” There are no papers. There is a tongue.
lhh.howrah.loafer_talk.ok: “Fine. Next time — papers.” He moves off, and you are still standing there, because of your knees.
lhh.howrah.loafer_talk.fail: “Name.” He writes your name in the book. Now you are in the book. He lets you go — but the book stays.
lhh.howrah.dcruz: “Ticket.” He takes it, holds it to the lamp, squints. “Name's smudged. Well, run along.”
lhh.howrah.dcruz.stage: Mr D'Cruz, ticket inspector, eighteen years on the gate. The only one who looks at your ticket and tries to read the name.
lhh.howrah.jumma: “Carry it, sahib? Two annas.” The coolie with the numbered badge already has your luggage by the strap. “For an extra anna — I'll tell you what they loaded on this train.”
lhh.howrah.jumma.extra: Three annas. Carry it and talk.
lhh.howrah.jumma.hired: He walks ahead, and the crowd parts before the badge as it never parted before you.
lhh.howrah.jumma.crate: “A crate. Sealed. Four guards, all white, loaded it at the head of the train at night. Nobody asked for a waybill.” He talks as he walks, not turning round. The first time you hear of it.
lhh.platform.text: The clock over the platform says {now}. The train left at half past eight — you can see the tail carriage slowly drawing away from the platform's edge. Porters, bundles, a woman seeing her son off to the regiment, a boy with a kettle, someone running alongside and not catching up.
lhh.platform.stage: The brake van is the last thing within reach. You have control for the whole run.
lhh.platform.gaskell: “Stand clear!” A whistle. The station master stands where he will stand at every station of this train — behind glass, outside.
lhh.platform.climb: Jump onto the nearest carriage and work along the footboards to the tail.
lhh.platform.run_straight: You run. The platform ends sooner than you thought.
lhh.platform.run_barrow: Barrow, leap, a shout behind you. You are on your feet and closer to the tail than you were.
lhh.platform.run_barrow_fail: The barrow tips, and you with it. Skinned palms. You get up and run — the platform has not ended yet.
lhh.platform.run_climb: Footboard, handrail, footboard. The carriages pass beneath you like steps. The brake van is the last.
lhh.platform.run_climb_fail: The handrail slips from your hand. You hang, then drop and run the last yards on foot, like everyone.
lhh.platform.dark: Darkness. Thunder. Hands and knees. The floor shakes, and you do not know which way is up.
ui.trial.title: The Dispute of the Clock
ui.trial.hours_lost: Regulator: {time} · rounds in a row: {streak} of {need}
ui.car02.stub: Car 2 — Third Class A. Built in M3.
co.dark: Darkness. Thunder. The floor shakes and slides from under your palms. Somewhere something drips, somewhere iron creaks.
co.dark.stage: The player on hands and knees. The first action in the game.
co.stand.out: You stand. Your feet find the floor, your back the wall. In the dark, at face height — the cold iron of a hook, and glass.
co.lantern: Take the lantern from the hook and light it.
co.lit: Light. In it: a sleeping man in uniform on a folding bunk, a stove, a wheel. The regulator clock: half past eight. Shelves of unclaimed luggage run back further than the length of the carriage allows.
co.silhouette: In the depth, where the light ends — a silhouette. Sitting. Not moving.
co.door: The front door is ajar by a palm's width. Beyond it is not a vestibule. Beyond it is daylight and a very great deal of space.
co.slam: Three seconds. A draught slams the door.
co.title: TEN HOURS EARLIER
ret.turn: Darkness, thunder, hands and knees. The same frame. Only the lantern is already lit, and the silhouette in the depth turns.
ret.with_monimala: Beside you on the floor — Monimala with the urn. She raises her head first. You are not alone in the first scene of this train.
ret.alone: Apart from the sleeping conductor and the silhouette — no one. You are alone, and the carriage knows it.
ret.not_passenger: “A passenger is one who sat down. You jumped. There is no name on the ticket. Tell me who is riding here.”
ret.not_passenger.stage: He does not stand. He taps the beat with the conductor's key on the stove — in time with the wheels.
trial.shani.intro: The dispute is not about whether you will be let through. It is about whether you exist on this train.
trial.shani.stage: Time stops: the wheels fall silent, dust hangs, the flame in the stove freezes. The colour goes.
trial.shani.check.name: Persuasion or Deception
trial.shani.critical: “The name is not missing. It is erased. That is another thing.”
trial.shani.critical.out: He falls silent. For the first time. The hand does not move, but the carriage shudders as if the train had been jerked by the tail. He knows — and now he knows that you know.
trial.shani.name.arg: “There is no name on the ticket. So there is no ticket.”
trial.shani.name.stage: He holds your ticket in two fingers, not looking.
trial.shani.name.find: Walk round the scene: the desk from another angle — the journal is open at the berth ledger.
trial.shani.name.persuade: “The ticket was sold to me. The name is the booking office's business, not mine.”
trial.shani.name.bahi: Present the bahi-khata: the name is in the account book.
trial.shani.name.shout: “I'm not a boy to answer to you!”
trial.shani.name.win: “The office.” He weighs the word like a coin and lays the ticket on the stove. The round is yours.
trial.shani.name.lose: “The office's business.” He nods — and turns the hand. There is no office here.
trial.shani.name.bahi.win: He reads the account book longer than the ticket. “Recorded. So you exist.” The round is yours.
trial.shani.name.shout.lose: The shout goes into the shelves and does not come back. He does not even raise his eyes. The hand goes back.
trial.shani.late.arg: “The latecomer does not ride. The latecomer stays.”
trial.shani.late.stage: He is not saying it to you. He is saying it to the clock.
trial.shani.late.find: Walk round the scene: the dial from behind — the hands at half past eight exactly. Not 20:31.
trial.shani.late.debt: “Lateness is a debt. A debt is paid, not stayed with.”
trial.shani.late.minutes: “I was a minute late. A minute!”
trial.shani.late.win: A pause one beat long. “Perhaps.” He does not turn the hand. The round is yours.
trial.shani.late.lose: “Not about me.” The hand goes back an hour, and the light in the carriage changes.
trial.shani.late.debt.win: He knows the price of a debt — you can see it in how he keeps silent. The round is yours.
trial.shani.late.minutes.lose: “A minute.” He looks at the clock standing at half past eight. “There are no minutes here.” The hand goes back.
trial.shani.haste.arg: “Where are you hurrying to? No one is waiting for you there.”
trial.shani.haste.stage: The scene is empty from any angle. There is nothing to find.
trial.shani.haste.find: Walk round the scene: nothing. That is the answer.
trial.shani.haste.argue_hard: “Where I'm hurrying is none of your business.”
trial.shani.haste.yield.win: You sit on the crate opposite. A beat, another beat. He nods — the only time you will ever see him nod. The round is yours.
trial.shani.haste.argue.lose: “Expected.” He says it so that the word loses its meaning. The hand goes back.
trial.shani.haste.argue_hard.lose: “Not my business.” He agrees — and turns the hand. To argue here was to lose.
trial.shani.hour.1: Half past seven. The light from the vestibule windows turns to sunset. The luggage on the top shelves is different.
trial.shani.hour.2: Half past six. The wind in the vestibule dies down. The stove is colder.
trial.shani.hour.3: Half past five. Bir Singh wakes, stands and makes his round, not seeing you.
trial.shani.hour.4: Half past four. Day. The shelves are shorter than they were: the unclaimed has not been brought yet.
trial.shani.hour.5: Half past three. Kanu is not here: he has not boarded yet. The carriage smells of paint.
trial.shani.hour.6: Half past two. The carriage is daylit, empty, standing on a siding. You are on the Howrah platform, a minute before departure.
trial.shani.clock_turn: He goes to the regulator and turns the hand back an hour. Gold — for one beat. Silence, wheels included. Then everything returns.
trial.shani.win: “You ride.” He puts the key away. The wheels come back first, then the dust falls, then the colour. Time moves.
trial.shani.soft_reset: You argued down to half past two. The carriage is daylit and empty, on a siding. Everything begins again — and this is neither death nor a load.
paths.hub_won: “A passenger. Good. There are two ways out: the engine and patience. Choose, but not in haste.”
paths.hub_lost: “A latecomer. No matter. There are two ways out: the engine and patience.”
paths.menu: The front door is locked not by a lock but by the conductor's decision. The shelves run into darkness. Stove, wheel, journal.
paths.deceit: Pass yourself off as someone allowed through.
paths.stay: Take the lantern from the hook.
paths.exit_lie: “The engine — there, ahead, through all the carriages. And patience — here.” He does not add that patience means taking his place.
paths.exit_lie.stage: A lie by omission, like everything he does.
force.door: The door. No lock, no bolt — only a decision. Shani sits on the crate and waits. He will not interfere. He will turn the clock.
force.door.stage: One hour for every two rounds of breaking.
force.strain: The door does not give. Shani looks at the clock. Your shoulder hums.
force.forced: The door comes off its hinges. Wind bursts into the carriage, luggage flies from the shelves. Shani does not stand. There will be no gift — and in a hundred hours you will come back through this door.
deceit.pick: Who will you claim to be?
deceit.relief_uniform: The relief conductor — in Bir Singh's uniform.
deceit.ok: “Relief.” He knows you are lying. He likes it. “Then relieve.”
deceit.ok.stage: He smiles for the first time. Not at you — at the situation.
deceit.gift: “Take it. An hour ago — once per journey. The vow: no haste. Hurry, and the hour will come back on its own, and not where you want.” The door is open.
deceit.fail: “No.” One word — and the hand goes back an hour.
deceit.fail.stage: He is not angry. He turns the clock.
service.offer_taught: Three tasks, as Ratan explained: the brake on the descent, the signal glasses, the inventory. You know what, and in what order.
service.offer_raw: Three tasks of the brake van. Nobody explained how: the wheel, the glasses, the journal — work it out as you go.
service.brake: The descent to the Hooghly. The engine will whistle three times; on each, a turn of the wheel on the beat.
service.brake.fail: Off the beat. The train jerks, luggage slides forward. The descent is not over yet.
service.brake.ok: Three whistles — three turns. The train runs smooth. Shani does not look, but listens.
service.lamps: The signal glasses at the tail. Red to the rear, green to the side — or the other way; a mistake will be seen two carriages on by an oncoming train.
service.lamps.wrong: The glasses are in. Something about them is wrong, but the tail is already behind and the oncoming train ahead. It will surface in chapter two.
service.lamps.ok: Red to the rear, green to the side. The tail reads correctly.
service.ledger: The inventory. Enter the unclaimed luggage in the journal — and read what is already written there.
service.ledger.ok: The inventory is completed in your hand. The journal is read.
service.complete: “The shift.” He stands — for the first time in all this while — and opens the door himself. A crow's feather and the gift: “An hour ago. Do not hurry.”
service.complete.stage: The best outcome. It cost an extra forty minutes.
service.opens: Beyond the door — night, wind and the wall of the next carriage.
stay.hook: The lantern on the hook. To take it and hang it on your belt is to hold.
stay.take: Take the lantern and hang it on your belt.
stay.question: “You will be the one holding. Do you understand what that means?”
stay.question.stage: One calm question. No “are you sure?” beyond it.
stay.hang_back: The lantern on the hook. The clock runs — that is, stands. As it was.
ending_5.title: THE LANTERN
ending_5.line_1: Shani goes silently into the depth, behind the shelves, where the light does not reach. The lantern is on your belt. The regulator clock stands at half past eight.
ending_5.line_2: The train will not arrive and will not explode. The moment is held — now by you. The brake van is empty until the next latecomer.
ending_5.line_3: This is the only ending without detonation. You have played less than one per cent of the game, and this was a choice available from the first hour.
ending_5.line_4: Leaving and stopping are equals from the very beginning.

credits.fiction_note: Dr Haren Mallick, the Anglo-Aryan Society and the Prana Union are fictional. The invention of the weapon is tied to no real scientist of the era.
transition.night_bengal.1: The outer door. Night, wind, Bengal going backwards past the window. The train does not slow.
transition.night_bengal.2: The handrail. Cold. The footboard under your foot, the carriage wall under your palm.
transition.night_bengal.3: Between the carriages — nothing. The coupling clanks below, sleepers flicker white.
transition.night_bengal.4: The wall of the next carriage. A rung, another rung. The door.
transition.night_bengal.5: Inside. Back to the door, breathing. The ritual is over.
transition.night_bengal_forced.1: The broken door bangs on its hinges. The wind goes through the carriage, luggage is scattered. Shani does not appear.
car_01.tail.forced_door: The door broken off, wind wandering, luggage scattered. Shani does not appear at all.
car_01.tail.shift_worked: The lamps burn as they should, the inventory is completed in your hand, tea on the desk.
car_01.tail.lantern_taken: There is no tail: this is an ending.
car_01.tail.clock_hours_lost: The clock shows the hour you argued down to, and the carriage is lit accordingly.
car_01.tail.default: The brake van as you left it: the lantern on the hook, the clock at half past eight, the silhouette in the depth.
kanu.boy: “Don't give me away. I'm quiet. I'm no trouble to anyone here.”
kanu.stage: A boy of about twelve in the depth of the shelves. Thin, quick, with a lathi.
kanu.three_months: “Third month. The train has never arrived, not once. I don't know any more if I want it to.” He says it calmly, like the weather.
kanu.shelves: “Everything nobody claimed. I know where what is. The sealed sack — second tier, the notebook — at the very end, where it's dark.”
kanu.lathi: He drinks a long time. Then holds out the lathi: “Take it. I don't need it here.”
ratan.stove: “Sit, warm yourself. The wheel — it's not for strength, it's for the beat.”
ratan.stage: Ratan Mondol, retired brake conductor, by the stove. Riding without a ticket to his daughter in Burdwan.
ratan.teach: “Three whistles — three turns, and never before the whistle. The glasses: red to the rear, green to the side, never the other way. The inventory — line by line, skipping none.” You remember.
ratan.burdwan: “A daughter. Grandchildren. A station the train…” He does not finish. He knows which station the train will not reach.
saraswati.tiffin: “I sat down for a minute. My husband's dinner. He's at the points, and the train moved. I'll get off at the first stop.”
saraswati.stage: Saraswati, a pointsman's wife, with tiffin boxes. The only one in the carriage who still believes she will get off.
saraswati.clock_fact: “At half past eight exactly, I was looking at the clock.” Exactly. Not 20:31. The train was leaving at the very moment you were running.
saraswati.clock_miss: “Half past eight, I think.” She isn't sure, and you don't catch why it matters.
hafiz.first: The old pilgrim sleeps sitting, beads in his hand. He does not answer.
hafiz.second: You speak again. The beads do not move. The chest does not rise. For a long time.
hafiz.dead: He is dead. Not a ghost — simply nobody noticed, and Yama has not reached him. Say it aloud?
hafiz.said: The carriage changes. Kanu cries. Shani stands — for the first time.
hafiz.kept: You keep silent. The beads in his hand. Ajmer ahead.
hafiz.named: Hafiz-sahib sits as he sat. Now everyone knows. Nobody comes near.
bir_singh.asleep: The real conductor sleeps on the folding bunk. His uniform, his lantern, his journal — but not him.
bir_singh.stage: Bir Singh. Asleep since half past eight.
bir_singh.no_wake: He does not wake. Not for three days — since half past eight. He can be woken only by force, and he will remember nothing.
bir_singh.took_uniform: The uniform is yours. He did not stir. Lying is easier in a relief conductor's uniform.
monimala.urn: “We made it.” The urn on her knees, warm. “Beyond that door is not a carriage. I saw.”
monimala.stage: Monimala Devi, the widow with the urn. The only one who can be brought into the first scene.
monimala.door.out: “Light. Daylight. And so much room you could get lost in it. I won't go there first.”
monimala.clock.out: “At half past eight. Exactly. I was looking at the clock while you ran.” The train was leaving at the very moment you were running.
dog.seals: The dog from the shrine. Lies by the sealed coffin and barks at the seal — short, without malice. It does not look at you.
npc.bir_singh.state.patrol: making his round, not seeing you
npc.kanu.state.default: in the depth of the shelves
mg.brake_wheel.title: Brake on the descent
mg.brake_wheel.intro: Three whistles from the engine. On each — a turn of the wheel on the beat.
mg.signal_lamps.title: Signal glasses
mg.signal_lamps.intro: Two lamps at the tail. Which glass goes where?
mg.ledger.title: Conductor's journal
mg.ledger.intro: The inventory of the unclaimed — line by line. And what is already written.
mg.ledger.entry_1: 14 October. Unclaimed luggage received, Howrah, 12 pieces. Seals intact.
mg.ledger.entry_2: Coffin under seal, waybill No. … Consignee's name illegible.
mg.ledger.entry_3: Departure 20:30. Tail lamps checked. Regulator clock set.
mg.ledger.entry_berths: Berth ledger. Car 2, compartment B: a name entered… and over it, another.
mg.ledger.smear: You look closer: the first name is not missing. It is erased. Over it — another.
mg.ledger.smear_fail: The ink has run, the line cannot be read. You turn the page.
item.seed_mail_sack.name: Mail sack
item.seed_mail_sack.desc: Seal unbroken. Addressed to the mail car.
item.seed_music_stand.name: Folding music stand
item.seed_music_stand.desc: Parsi theatre, Bombay. The score on it is not in English.
item.seed_opium_crate.name: Crate with Patna markings
item.seed_opium_crate.desc: Number painted over. Smells the way the Salkia warehouses smell.
item.seed_shackle_lock.name: Shackle lock
item.seed_shackle_lock.desc: No shackles. No key. Kala Pani.
item.seed_child_shoe.name: Child's shoe
item.seed_wire_spool.name: Spool of telegraph wire
item.seed_wire_spool.desc: A hundred feet. A telegraphist knows what to do with it.
item.seed_regiment_drum.name: Regimental drum
item.seed_calipers_box.name: Box of anthropometric calipers
item.seed_census_forms.name: Census forms
item.seed_census_forms.desc: Blank. The ‘occupation’ column is wider than the rest.
item.seed_ice_box.name: Ice box
item.seed_ice_box.desc: A puddle beneath it. Boston ice, if the stamp is to be believed.
item.seed_zenana_shawl.name: Woman's shawl
item.seed_zenana_shawl.desc: A zenana laundry mark. Not for here.
item.seed_mallick_notebook.name: Notebook of calculations
item.seed_mallick_notebook.desc: Calculations that do not add up. It can be taken in the first hour. Understood in the eightieth.
item.conductor_lantern.name: Conductor's lantern
item.conductor_lantern.desc: On the hook. To take it and hang it on your belt is to hold the moment. Unique.
item.conductor_uniform.name: Conductor's uniform
item.conductor_uniform.desc: Bir Singh's. For one who wants to pass as the relief.
item.morse_key.name: Morse key
item.morse_key.desc: From the luggage. No wire. Yet.
item.lamp_oil.name: Lamp oil
item.matches.name: Matches
item.chagul.name: Water-skin
item.chagul.desc: A leather flask. The water is warm.
item.lathi.name: Lathi
item.lathi.desc: Kanu's bamboo staff. He'll give it for food.
item.crystal_cutter.name: Crystal cutter
item.crystal_cutter.desc: One charge. Cuts what will not open.
item.vahana_crow_feather.name: Crow's feather
item.vahana_crow_feather.desc: Shani's vahana. See the tunnel timer; −2 to initiative.
item.gift_hour_ago.name: The gift “An Hour Ago”
item.gift_hour_ago.desc: Once per game, undo the last scene and replay it. The vow: no haste.
item.small_prana_crystal.name: Small prana crystal
item.small_prana_crystal.desc: Three charges. Real, from Ah Sun.
item.fake_prana_crystal.name: Glass fake
item.fake_prana_crystal.desc: Fools a detector once. Not twice.
